clue.text: Post letters for Switzerland in different nations

indicators.note: the Swiss letters are placed in among the rearranged letters
different nations means the letters of the word nations made different, rearranged

parts.note: CH, for Confoederatio Helvetica, is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A post office dealing with mail from Switzerland across several countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' signals the anagram, giving STANION, and 'in' signals the insertion. Post looks like mail beside 'letters', but it is an upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright bar or support, the same thing as a post.

clue.text: Issue one cent coins for circulation? Carrying on thus — within reason — I create a sort of boom

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Issue one cent coins for circulation? Carrying on thus — within reason — I create a sort of boom', carries three separate wordplays (SON+I+C, an anagram of coins, and a run inside 'reason I create') for one definition; the grammar takes only one, so 'coins for circulation' and 'Carrying on thus' would be left doing nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Issue one cent coins for circulation? Carrying on thus — within reason — I create a sort of boom

clue.text: Garage repaired tank entering compound

indicators.note: the word for a tank goes inside the rearranged letters
something repaired is put back together, so the letters of garage are reassembled

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: A garage mechanic fixes a tank that has rolled into a military compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' gives AGGRAE and 'entering' signals the insertion. 'compound' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb meaning make worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To compound a problem is to make it worse, which is what aggravating it does.

clue.text: Singer-songwriter in Wenceslas Square, finally?

indicators.note: the final letter of square is placed in the middle of the description of Wenceslas

parts.note: Good King Wenceslas is the king of a famous Christmas carol, so he is a carol king

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word square

explanation.surface: A singer performing in Prague's Wenceslas Square at the end of a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Wenceslas is the king in the Christmas song 'Good King Wenceslas'; 'in' puts the last letter of Square between the two words describing him. Wenceslas Square is a real square in Prague, which disguises the device.
explanation.definitionFit: Carole King is an American singer-songwriter, known for the album Tapestry.

clue.text: Current not carrying snake up the creek

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

indicators.note: the word not holds the snake inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: taken as written
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A river current that, without its snake, leaves someone stranded upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' signals the insertion, making NASPOT. 'up the creek' can look like a direction for reversal in a down clue, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up the creek is an idiom for being in trouble, as is being in a spot.

clue.text: Potential nuns may be turned on by bad habits

indicators.note: turned means the little word on is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: vices are bad habits

explanation.surface: Trainee nuns who might be tempted by naughty behaviour, playing on a nun's habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes NO from ON. Habits looks like the nuns' clothing, but here it means behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are people in the trial period before taking religious vows, so they may become nuns.

clue.text: Run male and female quarters

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Running a building with separate rooms for men and women.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's part of a Muslim household, kept apart from the men.

clue.text: Divine consort from another age

indicators.note: from tells you the letters are taken out of the words another age

explanation.surface: A goddess's partner who belongs to a different era.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the Greek goddess who is the wife of Zeus, king of the gods.

clue.text: Rubbish ends in English river

indicators.note: ends picks the first and last letters of the word rubbish

explanation.surface: Litter has finished up in an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a great European river flowing through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: Office in springtime said to have emptied tea trolley

parts.note: May is a month in spring
oral means spoken, said aloud

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside of the phrase tea trolley, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: The spring office party where the tea trolley was cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' takes the inside out of 'tea trolley', leaving T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoralty is the office of a mayor, or the term in which they hold it.

clue.text: Not the last reversal for queen and country

indicators.note: reversal means the shortened word is read backwards
not the last means the final letter of the word for queen is dropped

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, used in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A queen suffers a final setback for her country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the last' cuts REGINA to REGIN, and 'reversal' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa.

clue.text: Notice perch in extremely hard times

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: the word for perch goes in the word for extremely

parts.note: very means extremely
to sit is to perch

explanation.surface: Hard times for a bird looking for somewhere to perch, as a notice says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion, making VERSITY. 'extremely hard' reads as one phrase, but 'extremely' is a piece and 'hard times' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity is misfortune or hardship, a period of hard times.

clue.text: Fawns walk in confined area

parts.note: to fawn is to grovel or crawl, so fawns gives crawls
to pace is to walk

explanation.surface: Young deer walking about in a small enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawns looks like the young deer, but here it is a verb meaning grovels.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawlspace is a low, cramped area under a floor or roof.

clue.text: Shoulder or stomach

definitions.meaning: to shoulder a burden is to carry it
to stomach something is to tolerate it

explanation.definitionFit: To bear means both to carry a load and to put up with something.

clue.text: What's yielding for bare bum?

indicators.note: yielding means giving way, so the letters of the following words give way and reform

explanation.surface: Asking what soft thing would suit a bare bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' rearranges FOR BARE BUM. The whole clue also asks what is soft enough for a bare bottom to sit on.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam rubber is soft, spongy material used in cushions that gives under pressure.

clue.text: Mouth of smiley supporter

definitions.meaning: in a typed smiley face :) the mouth is a closing round-ended mark
a shelf support fixed to a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A bracket is a typed mark that forms the smiley's mouth, and also a wall support for a shelf.

clue.text: Hotel owner is seen with a thousand small lizards

parts.note: Basil Fawlty runs the hotel in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A hotelier spotted with lots of tiny lizards about the place.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s British TV comedy about a rude hotel owner, Basil Fawlty.
explanation.definitionFit: Basilisks are tropical American lizards, named after the mythical serpent.

clue.text: Unhappy Social Democrat finally resigned

indicators.note: unhappy suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged
finally points to the last letter of the word democrat

explanation.surface: A miserable Social Democrat politician has finally quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy' rearranges SOCIAL plus T, the last letter of Democrat. 'resigned' looks like quitting a post, but here it means accepting things calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stoical means accepting hardship patiently, as one is resigned to one's fate.

clue.text: Liberace is disheartened after very bad record

indicators.note: after puts the remains of the pianist's name behind the word for very bad

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad

indicators.note: disheartened takes the heart out of the name Liberace, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: The flamboyant pianist Liberace is downcast after a dreadful recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves LE, the outer letters of Liberace.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written account of events in order, a historical record.

clue.text: Bone from tail of flightless bird? I'm not sure

indicators.note: tail of picks the last letter of the word flightless

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Wondering whether this bone comes from the tail of an emu or an ostrich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail of flightless bird' reads as one idea, but the tail belongs to 'flightless' alone, and 'bird' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone in the middle of the chest.

clue.text: Wealth that is retained for those lacking generosity

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is is kept inside the word for wealth

parts.note: means, as in a person of means, are money or wealth
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Rich people who hang on to their money are mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retained' signals the insertion. Wealth and generosity sit together in the surface, but only the second phrase defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanies is an informal word for stingy or unkind people.

clue.text: Simple soldiers at ease outside

indicators.note: the word for at ease sits outside the soldiers

parts.note: comfy means comfortable, at ease
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers relaxing outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: an old word for a medicinal herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old name for a medicinal plant, and comfrey is one such healing herb.

clue.text: Slim Pickens finally entering church free from sin

indicators.note: the thin word and the last letter go into the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
lean means slim

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name Pickens

explanation.surface: The actor Slim Pickens finally goes into church to be absolved.
explanation.walkthrough: Slim Pickens was an American actor, so Slim looks like part of his name, but it is a piece meaning thin; 'entering' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to purify or make free of sin.

clue.text: A lot of porridge or just a bowl of cherries?

definitions.meaning: porridge is British slang for prison time
from the song saying this is just a bowl of cherries

explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is a long spell in jail, and the song says existence is just a bowl of cherries.

clue.text: Criminal found with ring?

definitions.meaning: a criminal who handles stolen goods
the word that follows ring in ring-..., a barrier enclosing an area

explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a receiver of stolen goods, and it joins ring to make ring-fence.

clue.text: After quiet period artist produces exciting work

indicators.note: after places the painter behind the letters for quiet and period

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an age is a period of time
J M W Turner was the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: An artist produces exciting work after a quiet spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a book so gripping you cannot stop reading.

clue.text: Lightning strike brings in first of pickets

indicators.note: the word for strike takes in the first letter of pickets

parts.note: a raid is a sudden strike or attack

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word pickets

explanation.surface: During a lightning strike, the first pickets are brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightning' and 'strike' look like a single storm, but 'Lightning' is the definition, an adjective meaning very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightning speed is extremely fast, so lightning is a fair synonym for rapid.

clue.text: Fish on film dropping a stick

indicators.note: dropping means the letter a is let fall from the fish's name

parts.note: A Fish Called Wanda is a 1988 comedy film

explanation.surface: A fish in a film loses its grip on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A wand is a thin stick, such as a magician's or conductor's baton.

clue.text: Feeling sorry for Estonians

indicators.note: sorry in the sense of sorry-looking, in a poor state, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Sympathy for the people of Estonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' rearranges ESTONIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a physical feeling, such as warmth or pain.

clue.text: Lancashire town providing support when king abdicates

indicators.note: a monarch who abdicates gives up the throne, so the letter for king leaves the word

parts.note: backup is support
K is king in chess

explanation.surface: A northern town that rallies round when the monarch gives up the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; Bacup is a small town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a market town in the Rossendale valley in Lancashire.

clue.text: Role for Patrick Macnee's horse

definitions.meaning: the actor played the bowler-hatted agent John in The Avengers
a horse, especially a spirited riding horse

explanation.definitionFit: John Steed was Macnee's character in the 1960s British TV series The Avengers, and a steed is a horse.

clue.text: Fashion parades in which male's taken lead

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the male pronoun
taken in by the reshaped word
to fashion is to shape, so the letters of parades are shaped anew

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Fashion shows in which a male model has taken the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' signals the anagram, giving SPEARAD, and 'in which ... taken' signals the insertion. Fashion parades suggests catwalk shows, which is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead something is to lead it from the front.
